mathematical_boundary: The intrinsic action fixes every specified speed without a degree bound on the last coordinate. The last coordinate's leading coefficient is also fixed when that degree is positive. The construction requires at least one nonzero speed; all-zero speeds are separately recognized.

For a quadratic last coordinate, q^2 lies in J in the actual invariant polynomial plane, and hence in its extensions to A and B. This does not imply q in J, q in I^2, reducedness, a polynomial shear solution or coordinate recognition.

Any first-power defect is supported on finitely many plane points where J is contained in the squared maximal ideal. No actual action with such a defect is constructed, and the bare monomial ideal is not one.

The intrinsic action may require further freeness analysis. The speed row is not automatically a unit row. Neither supplied-frame recognition in full generality nor unrestricted frame entry is proved.
